core_takeaways: Photography quality must start from capture logic: light, lens, pose, crop, background and product placement before retouching.
Portrait retouching should preserve skin texture, identity and light direction; plastic smoothing is a failure pattern.
Product photography depends on controlled background, readable edge contour, label accuracy, material texture and reflection management.
Composition optimization is a correction layer with geometry constraints, not a license to stretch bodies, products or architecture.
Hanfu portraits need costume, hair, makeup, prop, scene, posture and light coherence as a full cultural styling system.
prompt_structure_lessons: Photography prompts must specify capture conditions before post-production edits.
Separate global color grade from local retouching instructions.
List exact retouch operations: blemish removal, skin texture, hair cleanup, clothing wrinkle, background cleanup, product edge, reflection, crop.
For Hanfu, lock dynasty/garment mood, location type, prop, pose and light before describing atmosphere.
For product images, lock label/source assets and forbid pseudo text.

risk_controls.mitigation: Use skin_texture_preserved and local-mask notes as mandatory quality gates.
Require supplied label assets or placeholders; treat pseudo-labels as failures.

risk_controls.risk: wrong light direction after background replacement
risk_controls.mitigation: Check subject shadow, catchlights, product contact shadow and background lighting as one system.
Lock costume-scene-prop-hair-makeup coherence before style language.
Use composition gates for eye line, hands, sleeves, product edge, horizon and verticals.
